title: Register-vector invariance of probabilistic semantics
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let $o$ be a Boolean parameter, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $B$ be a natural-number register bound, let $l$ be a control label, let $p$ be rational, let $\sigma'$ be a register state, and let $f$ be a function from the fifteen register indices to the natural numbers. If $f$ is the register vector of $\sigma'$ and the polynomial-amplification program, started at $l$ with register vector $\sigma'$ and no result, has every register at most $B$, terminates for every sequence of choice bits, and returns true and false with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively, for every number of choice bits for which every branch terminates, then the abstract program has the same termination and probability properties when started at $l$ with register vector $f$ and no result.
hypotheses_covered: finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
function $f$ from fifteen register indices to natural numbers
